clue.text: Late shop?

parts.note: surface reading: a shop that stays open late into the evening
setter's reading: 'the late' are the dead, so this is a business that serves them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' suggests opening hours, but it means deceased; the question mark flags the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertaker's premises where bodies of the recently deceased are prepared and viewed is a business devoted to the dead.

clue.text: Guerrilla fed eight former members badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched and disordered, so the preceding words are jumbled

parts.note: the fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A rebel band feeding eight ex-members poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' adds nothing to the letters; it only finishes the surface picture of former members of a band.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerrilla is an irregular soldier waging war against a regime, which supporters describe as fighting for liberty.

clue.text: Good book for figures

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a book of the Bible, the Good Book
second meaning: digits used for counting

explanation.surface: A recommended read about numerals or statistics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good book' reads as praise for any book, but the Good Book is the Bible, and this is its fourth book.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth book of the Old Testament carries this title, and the plain word also means digits or numerals.

clue.text: Get up around noon and wash

indicators.note: one word goes around another, enclosing it in its middle

parts.note: to get up is to rise

explanation.surface: A lazy morning routine: get out of bed at midday and have a wash.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse something is to clean it lightly with water, a quick wash.

clue.text: Weariness of girl, one performing duet

indicators.note: performing a piece means working it over, so its letters are put through a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A singer worn out from performing a duet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is physical or mental tiredness, a listless lack of energy.

clue.text: See 1
Spike has name in programme

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: prog is a short form of programme

explanation.surface: Spike, perhaps a person, gets a name-check in a TV programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Spike looks like a person's nickname appearing on a show, but it is the pointed object being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A prong is a pointed tine, as on a fork, so it is a kind of spike.

clue.text: Modern university doctor admitted lying down

indicators.note: someone admitted is let inside, so these pieces go within the other word

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A new university doctor was let in, as if admitted to a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Recumbent describes a body reclining or lying flat rather than upright.

clue.text: Fruit in very big field

indicators.note: one word placed in another is wrapped by it

parts.note: OS is short for outsize, very big
a range is a field or scope

explanation.surface: Fruit growing in a huge field.
explanation.walkthrough: OS for outsize is a clothing-size label, often used for very big.
explanation.definitionFit: Oranges are citrus fruits, so the plural noun fits the general word for produce.

clue.text: Crying for subdued wear to topless bars?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: weeping, overcome with emotion
second meaning, read literally: clothing cut down until only rips remain, fit for a topless bar

explanation.surface: Choosing muted clothing to wear to a strip club.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase is clothing reduced to tears, meaning cut down to rips; the question mark flags this playful second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone brought so low that they weep is commonly said to be pushed to the point of crying by distress.

clue.text: Hermit endlessly rejected Indonesian buyer's furs

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is read backwards
without ends means the first and last letters of the word are dropped

parts.note: the sen is a small Indonesian coin, money being what buys

explanation.surface: A recluse turned down furs offered by an Indonesian purchaser.
explanation.walkthrough: The sen is a hundredth of an Indonesian rupiah; calling a coin a buyer is a playful touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermine is the white winter fur of the stoat, prized for robes, so ermines are furs.

clue.text: Fruit supplier made love to cleaner in street!

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: one word set in another lies inside it

parts.note: RD is short for road, a street
a char is a cleaning lady

explanation.surface: A greengrocer who had a fling with the cleaner out in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: A char, or charwoman, is a British word for a hired cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plantation of fruit trees, so it supplies apples, pears and the like.

clue.text: Increasing exercises, needing to run around

indicators.note: the scrambled word goes around the other piece, enclosing it
letters set to run are loosed from their order and scattered

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Stepping up a workout that requires going for a run.
explanation.definitionFit: Deepening means growing more intense or profound, so it serves as a synonym of growing or intensifying.

clue.text: Charming old lady caught embracing US soldier

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so these letters wrap around the next piece

parts.note: one's old lady is one's mother, ma
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An elderly woman found hugging an American serviceman: a charming scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic as an adjective means enchanting or wonderful, the same spellbinding sense as charming.

clue.text: I reckon to retire with 100 to score

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: to sum is to reckon up

explanation.surface: A cricketer musing on retiring with a century to his name.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a batsman reaching 100 before quitting, but score is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is the written notation of a composition, the printed form of a piece's melody and harmony.

clue.text: Food Colin cooked and Anne consumed

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or tampered with, so the names' letters are reworked
eaten and broken down, so the second name joins the jumble too

explanation.surface: A couple at dinner: Colin prepares the meal and Anne eats it.
explanation.definitionFit: Canneloni are large pasta tubes stuffed and baked in sauce, an Italian dish.

clue.text: One Parisian prepared to be stripped

parts.note: dressed food, like a dressed crab, is prepared

explanation.surface: A Parisian getting ready to strip off.
explanation.definitionFit: Undressed means having had one's clothes taken off, naked, the same as stripped.

clue.text: Loathing pigs, Enid's going mad!

indicators.note: something going mad runs wild and loses its order

parts.note: the letters taken as written, the possessive S included

explanation.surface: Enid hates pigs so much it's sending her mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Despising means regarding with contempt, holding in strong dislike, a near match for hating.

clue.text: They show off flat and nurse shudders!

indicators.note: a shudder shakes things, and shaken letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: Showy types in a flat make the nurse wince.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaunters are people who display their possessions or looks ostentatiously, a noun matching show-offs.

clue.text: See 1
Medical condition I mean to raise in Alcoholics Anonymous

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something means reading it upward, backwards
one piece placed in another is enclosed by it

explanation.surface: Someone at an AA meeting wanting to bring up a health problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaemia is a deficiency of red blood cells or haemoglobin, a recognised illness causing fatigue.

clue.text: Brown tin-opener, one intrinsic flaw

indicators.note: split as in-trinsic, it puts the single letter inside
the opener of a word is the letter it starts with

parts.note: the leading letter of the word

explanation.surface: A brown can-opener with one built-in defect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tin-opener' looks like a kitchen gadget but asks for the opening letter of tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A taint is a trace of something bad, a blemish or defect that spoils.

clue.text: Top in frozen foods all over the polar regions

indicators.note: one word placed in another sits within it

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid

explanation.surface: The best frozen foods are found right across the Arctic and Antarctic.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice caps are permanent sheets of ice spread across the Arctic and Antarctic, covering those regions.

clue.text: See 8
When reversing car in, say a prayer

indicators.note: reversing goes backwards, so the assembled letters are read from the end
the vehicle word is put in the middle of the other

explanation.surface: A nervous driver says a prayer while backing the car in.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace is the short prayer of thanks said before or after a meal.

clue.text: Least tight, less loose

indicators.note: letters set loose are freed from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A play on degrees of slackness: least tight, less loose.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites reading as a comparison of tightness, with loose as an opposite, but loose only signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The slightest amount is the smallest possible, which is what least means as an adjective.

clue.text: Shoot second person, to be precise

parts.note: a prig is a priggishly precise, self-righteous person

explanation.surface: An order to shoot the second person, with an insistence on accuracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' reads as an order to fire, but it is the noun for a young twig.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small stem or twig with leaves, a young shoot of a plant.

clue.text: Monster water outlet conservationists overlooked

indicators.note: something overlooked is left out, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: a fire hydrant is a street water outlet
the National Trust, a British heritage conservation body

explanation.surface: Environmentalists missed a monstrous water outlet.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that conserves historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hydra is the many-headed serpent of Greek legend slain by Heracles, a mythical beast.

clue.text: Millions in club backed our embroidery

indicators.note: backed means moved back, so the word is read from the end
one letter placed in a word sits inside it

explanation.surface: A club that put millions behind our needlework project.
explanation.definitionFit: Tambour is embroidery worked on a drum-shaped frame, and the name covers both frame and stitching.

clue.text: State home help returns to North America

indicators.note: something that returns comes back the way it came, so it is read backwards

explanation.surface: A domestic helper heads back to America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home help' looks like a single phrase for a carer, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty United States, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Studying good girls may improve one's looks

parts.note: reading a subject is studying it

explanation.surface: Bookish nice girls might find it makes them more attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looks' suggests appearance; read as acts of looking, it is what spectacles help with.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles for close work sharpen the wearer's sight, so they improve how well one looks at a page.

clue.text: See 27
